# Time series basics

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

print("=== Time Series Basics ===\n")

print("Time series data has a time component.")
print("""
Components:
  ✅ Trend: Long-term direction
  ✅ Seasonality: Regular patterns
  ✅ Cyclical: Longer-term patterns
  ✅ Noise: Random fluctuations
""")

print("\n=== Creating Time Series Data ===\n")

np.random.seed(42)

# Create date range
dates = pd.date_range('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31', freq='D')
n = len(dates)

# Create time series components
time = np.arange(n)
trend = 10 + 0.01 * time  # Upward trend
seasonal = 5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * time / 30)  # Monthly seasonality
noise = np.random.normal(0, 2, n)

# Combine components
data = trend + seasonal + noise

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Date': dates,
    'Value': data
})

print(f"Time series shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Date range: {df['Date'].min()} to {df['Date'].max()}")
print(df.head(10))

print("\n=== Visualizing Time Series ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], linewidth=1)
plt.title('Time Series Data')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Decomposing Time Series ===\n")

from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose

# Decompose the time series
result = seasonal_decompose(df['Value'], model='additive', period=30)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(14, 10))

# Original
axes[0].plot(df['Date'], df['Value'])
axes[0].set_title('Original')

# Trend
axes[1].plot(df['Date'], result.trend)
axes[1].set_title('Trend')

# Seasonal
axes[2].plot(df['Date'], result.seasonal)
axes[2].set_title('Seasonal')

# Residual
axes[3].plot(df['Date'], result.resid)
axes[3].set_title('Residual')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rolling Statistics ===\n")

# Rolling mean (smoothing)
df['Rolling_Mean_7'] = df['Value'].rolling(7).mean()
df['Rolling_Mean_30'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).mean()

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_Mean_7'], label='7-day average')
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_Mean_30'], label='30-day average')
plt.title('Rolling Statistics')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Lag and Autocorrelation ===\n")

# Create lagged features
for lag in [1, 7, 30]:
    df[f'Lag_{lag}'] = df['Value'].shift(lag)

# Autocorrelation
from pandas.plotting import autocorrelation_plot

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
autocorrelation_plot(df['Value'])
plt.title('Autocorrelation Plot')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Time Series Patterns ===\n")

print("""
Patterns to look for:
  ✅ Trend: Upward or downward movement
  ✅ Seasonality: Regular recurring patterns
  ✅ Cyclical: Longer-term patterns (>1 year)
  ✅ Noise: Random variation
  ✅ Autocorrelation: Relationship with past values
""")

🐍 **Time series data has a temporal component.**

**Time series components:**
- **Trend**: Long-term direction
- **Seasonality**: Regular patterns
- **Cyclical**: Longer-term patterns
- **Noise**: Random variation

**Key operations:**
```python
# Rolling statistics
df['rolling_mean'] = df['value'].rolling(window=7).mean()
df['rolling_std'] = df['value'].rolling(window=7).std()

# Lags
df['lag_1'] = df['value'].shift(1)
df['lag_7'] = df['value'].shift(7)

# Differencing (remove trend)
df['diff'] = df['value'].diff()

# Decomposition
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose
result = seasonal_decompose(df['value'], model='additive', period=30)
```
